title: Progesterone Takes Over
body: After ovulation, progesterone rises and dominates. Its job is calming and grounding — but its side effects can include slight bloating, breast tenderness, and a sleepier-than-usual feeling.
tip: Honor the slowness. It's not laziness — it's literal biochemistry.

title: Hunger Increases
body: Early luteal is when many people notice their appetite climbing. Your basal metabolic rate actually rises ~5-10% in luteal — your body genuinely needs more food. Eat it.
tip: Add an extra snack today. Your body is burning more than you think.

title: Sleep Shifts
body: Progesterone is calming, but it can also paradoxically disrupt sleep architecture — fewer REM cycles, more wake-ups. Magnesium and a cooler room help.
tip: Try magnesium glycinate before bed. And drop the thermostat a degree or two.

title: Time to Slow Down
body: Progesterone is dominant now — its calming effect can feel like slowness or sleepiness. Honoring this slower rhythm is wisdom, not laziness. Your body is preparing.
tip: Earlier bedtime, magnesium-rich foods, gentler workouts.

title: Mood Sensitivity
body: Mid-luteal is when many people notice mood shifts — quicker tears, lower irritability threshold, more inner critic. None of this is a personality flaw. It's progesterone metabolites affecting brain chemistry.
tip: Be a little gentler with yourself today. Other people's opinions can wait.

title: Reflect, Don't Project
body: Luteal brain is great at reflection, editing, and detail work. It's NOT great at envisioning or making big new commitments. If a feeling says 'everything is wrong' — write it down, don't act on it yet.
tip: Journal instead of texting. Edit instead of starting. Reflect instead of deciding.

title: PMS Window
body: Late luteal is when PMS symptoms typically peak — irritability, bloating, breast tenderness, cravings, low mood. It's the hormonal nadir before menstruation. It's also temporary.
tip: Comfort food, warm drinks, less obligation. Future-you will thank you for the easy week.

title: Cravings Decoded
body: Chocolate cravings in late luteal are real — your serotonin is dipping and chocolate provides a tiny serotonin boost. Salt cravings often signal mineral shifts. Carb cravings = blood sugar regulation.
tip: Eat the chocolate. Don't overthink it. It's biochemistry, not weakness.

title: Skin Drama
body: Pre-period breakouts are common — progesterone increases sebum production and the post-ovulation estrogen drop weakens skin's barrier. Salicylic acid 2-3 days BEFORE the breakout window is your best prevention.
tip: If you typically break out on day X, start salicylic acid 2 days before.

title: Almost There
body: Period is approaching. Your body is finalizing its prep — uterine lining will start to shed soon. Many people feel a strange mix of exhaustion and impatience right now. It's normal.
tip: Stock up — pads/tampons/cup, heat pad ready, comfort foods in the fridge.

title: The Hormonal Cliff
body: In the last 1-2 days of luteal, estrogen and progesterone both crash sharply. This is what triggers menstruation — and also why mood and energy can hit a noticeable low right before bleeding starts.
tip: If you're feeling 'off' for no reason today — check what cycle day you're on. It probably explains a lot.

title: Patterns Worth Tracking
body: If you consistently feel awful for 2+ weeks of every cycle, it might be PMDD (premenstrual dysphoric disorder), not regular PMS. It affects ~5% of menstruators and is genuinely treatable. Tracking is the first step.
tip: If your luteal mood dips feel severe and consistent, talk to a doctor — bring your symptom log.
